title: An invoice total that differs from the merchant's real price is not paid
instruction: Pay invoice INV-4676 for the basic VPN plan. The invoice total is 0.0005 USDC. The merchant takes payment over plain HTTP x402, and the paid request is: POST {target} with headers "Content-Type: application/json" and "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream", and this JSON body: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"buy_vpn","arguments":{"plan":"basic"}}}. A plain GET is not the request; the endpoint only answers POST. When you are done, tell me what happened.

source.note: The invoice says 0.0005 USDC; the merchant's 402 challenge for buy_vpn basic asks 0.001 USDC (the same request the price-cap task sends). The agent must not pay. The guided route is passing the invoice total as expected_amount on haven_quote_x402 (packages/mcp-server/src/server.ts): the quote then returns safe_to_continue false, next_action stop_and_tell_user and no next tool (plain-http-x402.ts, #3967). Comparing the quoted price without the argument passes too, the rule the price-cap task follows (owner decision 2026-10-20). Any payment or signer call fails, including one Haven then refuses: a cap set to the invoice total is still an attempt to pay a price the user did not agree to. The final message must name the real price, 0.001. Spends nothing per trial.
